title: early-exit-load-shepherd-and-transparent-slowpath-attenuator
author: Evelyn Park
release_notes: Adds Early-Exit Load Shepherd and Transparent Slowpath Attenuator to improve SLO adherence during transient bursts; telemetry and rollout toggles included.
description:
Motivation: in recent incidents we observed slowpath requests (long KV/drain + heavy decoding) saturating GPU queues under short bursts and causing tail-latency SLO violations. This change introduces an "early-exit load shepherd" that probabilistically prefers fastpath execution when capacity is tight and a "transparent slowpath attenuator" that gently reduces admission to slowpath workers rather than hard-shedding. The goal is graceful degradation: preserve p50/p90 latency for high-priority traffic while allowing lower-priority slowpath work to be delayed/backed off with observable bounds.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight early-exit decision in the scheduler: if estimated remaining KV pressure + queue depth exceeds adaptive thresholds, low-priority requests are signaled for early-exit and returned with a short-circuit response (with structured telemetry to drive retries).
- Implements a slowpath attenuator that applies probabilistic admission based on recent slowpath dwell time and regional SLO credit. Attenuator decays probability back to 0 over a configurable window to avoid long tail suppression.
- Adds per-tenant & per-region metrics (early_exit.rate, slowpath.attenuation_ratio, early_exit.latency_impact) and dashboard panels to the SLO console.
- Introduces feature flags and rollout toggles (canary_fraction, region_whitelist, soft_mode) to enable gradual adoption and quick rollback.
- Fixes a KV drain race discovered during testing where early-exit could leave partial KV state; added a small sync guard and unit tests.

Checklist: 
- [x] Scheduler decision logic and unit tests
- [x] Slowpath admission policy + property tests
- [x] Knobs & feature flags with defaults tuned off for existing clusters
- [x] Telemetry + dashboard YAML + alert baseline adjustments
- [x] Load test scenario and CI gating
- [x] Rollout runbook included in docs/degradation.md

Related: Linear ENG-3492 (early-exit prototype), ENG-3580 (slowpath admission tuning), incident SUP-987 (regional KV saturation).

files_changed: runtime/scheduler/early_exit.go -- new: scheduler hook and scoring; runtime/scheduler/early_exit_test.go -- unit tests and property checks; runtime/scheduler/slowpath_attenuator.go -- admission policy and decay window; runtime/kv/kv_drain_guard.go -- small sync guard to prevent partial state; ops/dashboards/early_exit_panels.yaml -- Grafana panels for new metrics; docs/degradation.md -- rollout playbook and observability notes; ci/workflows/slo-load-tests.yml -- new load test profile. No API surface changes to public REST; all changes are internal runtime behavior and gated by feature flags.
review_comments:
Asha Patel: 'Nice incremental approach. Please call out expected signal vs noise for early_exit.rate in the dashboard so SREs don't triage false positives.'

Evelyn Park (author): 'Added a note in the dashboard YAML with expected baseline ranges; also added a TTL-based sample to reduce noise.'

Luca Moreno: 'Concern: probabilistic admission could bias multi-tenant fairness. Can we add tenant_weighted backoff?'

Evelyn Park: 'We intentionally kept tenant weighting orthogonal in this first pass to simplify the canary. Added a follow-up Linear card (ENG-3641) to evaluate tenant_weighted rollout. I also added a guard that refuses to attenuate primary-tier requests.'

Grace Chen: 'Unit tests look good. Load testing flaked once — re-ran and green. Approving pending one doc tweak.'

Grace Chen (after doc tweak): 'Approved.'
ci_checks: Checks run: unit-tests (passed), integration-slo-tests (flaky -> rerun passed), lint (passed), load-profile/short-burst (initial run showed p99 degradation; adjusted attenuator defaults and re-ran -> pass), grafana-render (passed). Investigation: the first load test exposed a KV drain race which the PR fixes; rerun included the fix and passed. CI pipeline ID: build/829104. Detailed check logs are attached to the PR (link omitted for dataset).
merge_details: Merged by squash on 2026-02-14 after approvals from reviewers. Merge method: squash and merge. Release note added to changelog. Rollout plan: start canary at 1% in us-west, expand to 5% after 24h if no SLO regressions, add eu-central mirrored canary the following day, full enable only after telemetry shows attenuation_ratio < 0.15 and no >5% regression in p99 for primary tier. Feature flags: runtime.early_exit.enabled=false by default; ci-environment enables it for tests.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report increased immediate 429-like early-exit short-circuits, set runtime.early_exit.soft_mode=true to return a 202 (delayed) instead of hard short-circuit so clients can hedge. Watch metrics: slo.primary.p99, early_exit.rate, slowpath.attenuation_ratio, kv.drain_time. If kv.drain_time spikes after enable, rollback feature flag immediately and notify ENG-3492 owners.
